::: {#exr-miller-deriv-product-chain-composite}
#### Combining product and chain rules

Adapted from @problifesavercalc, Question 1.1.7.

Find the derivative of

$$f(x) = \exp{x^8}\cos(3x^4)$$
:::

::: {#sol-miller-deriv-product-chain-composite}
Apply the product rule (@thm-product-rule) to $u(x) = \exp{x^8}$ and $v(x) = \cos(3x^4)$:

$$f'(x) = u'(x)v(x) + u(x)v'(x)$$

Compute $u'(x)$ and $v'(x)$ via the chain rule (@thm-chain-rule):

$$\ba
u'(x) &= 8x^7 \exp{x^8}
\\
v'(x) &= -12x^3 \sin(3x^4)
\ea$$

Substitute both derivatives into the product rule:

$$\ba
f'(x) &= 8x^7 \exp{x^8}\cos(3x^4) - 12x^3 \exp{x^8}\sin(3x^4)
\\
&= 4x^3 \exp{x^8}\sb{2x^4 \cos(3x^4) - 3\sin(3x^4)}
\ea$$
:::
